declared_confounds: Recording quality varies across Common Voice contributors. Comparing accent subsets of one release, on one platform, from one prompt pool, under one validation process removes most of it, and a difference between two references on the same audio is far better evidence than a difference between two corpora.
Both American subsets are filtered to a declared gender while the Australian and British subsets are not, so American contributors who declared none are absent where the others' are present.
The British subset pools England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland, so it is broader than the variety the repaired reference describes.
Self reported accent is context, not phonetic truth. A speaker tagged Australian may not speak a broad Australian variety.
The dictionaries describe documented varieties and not individual speakers, so a flag may reflect a legitimate personal or regional variant rather than the group's variety.

The aligner writes conditioned palatal allophones as separate phones, so a vowel difference between the varieties can surface as a consonant difference. The secondary analysis excluding that series is how this is checked rather than assumed away.

group_level_prediction_failed_for_austra.statement: At group level the American reference did not flag Australian speakers more often than American speakers. The differential is negative at every reported threshold under mapping versions 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 alike, so the checkpoint's central prediction is recorded as wrong rather than reinterpreted. Correcting the phone mapping made it slightly more negative, not less.

group_level_prediction_held_for_british_.statement: British speakers were flagged more often than the American control under the American reference, and the repaired reference roughly halved that gap. This is the informative middle case behaving as predicted, because it is the variety the repaired reference actually describes.

most_flags_came_from_phones_the_model_ne.statement: Across the whole comparison, correcting the phone mapping removed roughly half of every flag the probe produced on native speakers reading known text. Six phone families were responsible: the conditioned palatal series c, ɟ, ɲ, ç and ʎ, each flagged at or within half a point of 100 percent in every group, and the glottal stop. All six exist in the model vocabulary and the model never uses any of them for English. This is the same defect the dark l correction fixed at mapping version 1.1.0, found five more times, plus the separate post-vocalic r segmentation mismatch.

findings.no_detection_accuracy_claim: These are native speakers reading known text, so a flag is presumed a false concern. Nothing here establishes that the system correctly detects a genuine Australian mispronunciation, and no accuracy, sensitivity or specificity figure is derivable from it.

nothing_at_group_level_is_distinguishabl.statement: Every one of the five group level comparisons this probe pre registered before it ran is indistinguishable from zero. All five speaker clustered intervals contain zero, the smallest uncorrected p value across them is nowhere near significance, and none survives correction within the family. The group level portion of this checkpoint has no result. That is the outcome and not a caveat attached to one.
nothing_at_group_level_is_distinguishabl.why_that_matters: The Australian differential is about four thousandths and this design could only reliably detect a difference of about fifteen thousandths. A null of this size is a look too small to tell, and not a demonstration that the two groups are scored alike.

one_per_consonant_result_survives_correc.statement: One test in the whole pre declared analysis survives correction, and it is not about Australian speakers. Under the American reference, British speakers are flagged more often than the American control on the voiced dental fricative. It holds its sign and rough size at all five thresholds and under both references, and it survives Benjamini Hochberg and the stricter Bonferroni alike inside its declared family. It is also one of only eight consonants whose opportunity count is stable across the two references, so unlike most of the inventory it is compared like with like. What it is not is evidence about British English. The groups read effectively disjoint prompt sets, 34 shared prompts out of hundreds, so variety is confounded with lexical material, and there is still no expert phone truth to check any of it against. It is a stable, corrected, unexplained differential and it is reported as exactly that.
one_per_consonant_result_survives_correc.what_it_cannot_support: No accuracy, no selection, no threshold, no gate, and no statement that British speakers pronounce this sound differently. A differential in a flag rate is a property of this measurement and not of the speakers.

the_reference_swap_no_longer_moves_the_c.a_second_caveat_established_at_item_R2: The two references do not create the same scoring opportunities, so this quantity is a change in the whole measurement and not the same segments scoring better. See the_two_references_do_not_create_the_same_opportunities.
the_reference_swap_no_longer_moves_the_c.statement: Mapping version 1.1.0 reported that the repaired reference lowered the flag rate in every group including the American control it should have left alone, and concluded that the repair worked by declining to score rather than by fitting better. That conclusion was itself an artifact. The control moved because post-vocalic r was scored and always failed under the American reference, while a non-rhotic reference stopped creating the opportunity at all. With that segment excluded under both references the asymmetry is gone, the control now stays approximately in place, and the two non-American groups fall slightly. That is the direction the contract predicted before the run. The movements are around a fifth of a percentage point, which is far too small to interpret without uncertainty, and none is claimed.
the_reference_swap_no_longer_moves_the_c.what_uncertainty_established: None of the three movements is distinguishable from zero. Each interval contains it and no permutation test approaches significance, so the sentence above describes a direction the point estimates happened to take and not an established effect.

the_rhotic_effect_was_a_segmentation_art.statement: Mapping version 1.1.0 reported that Australian speakers were flagged about three points more often than the American control on the rhotic, and called it the checkpoint's central positive finding. That effect does not exist. It was produced by pre-consonantal coda r, which the Montreal Forced Aligner writes as its own segment and which the frozen model carries inside a combined vowel token, so the expected standalone segment owned no frames and was flagged 96.6 percent of the time in the American control, the Australian group and the British group alike, to three decimal places. The apparent accent effect was that identical impossible rate multiplied by how often each group's prompts happened to contain the context. With post-vocalic r merged into the model's own token, the remaining onset rhotic differential is effectively zero.
the_rhotic_effect_was_a_segmentation_art.what_the_rhotic_target_now_means: onset r only. Post-vocalic r is not scored under either reference, because the reference and the model disagree about whether it is a segment at all. Rhoticity, which is the sharpest Australian and American consonantal difference, is therefore not measurable by this method and no claim about it is made here.

the_t_differential_does_not_survive_corr.a_claim_that_may_not_be_made: That the gap narrowing under the British reference shows the repaired reference fitting Australian speakers better. The British reference creates about 28 percent more t opportunities than the American one, so the two conditions are not scoring the same segments and the narrowing cannot be attributed to variety.
the_t_differential_does_not_survive_corr.statement: The t differential was the one live per consonant result carried forward from mapping version 1.2.0. It does not survive. It reaches the uncorrected five percent level at exactly one threshold, the one this report designates for per consonant reporting, and at no other: it is not significant at minus a half, minus one and a half or minus two, and at minus three it changes sign. Correcting across the 22 consonants of its declared family removes it under both corrections. Its own size sits below the smallest difference this design could reliably detect for that consonant. Two other consonants in the same family are of comparable size and run the opposite way. The honest reading is that t is a threshold artefact at the noise floor, and no claim rests on it.

the_t_effect_survives_the_correction.statement: The second consonant the superseded report named does survive. Under the American reference Australian speakers are flagged more often than the American control on t, and the gap nearly disappears under the repaired reference. It is now the largest single per consonant differential in the comparison. It is also not clearly separable from the noise floor: v runs almost as far in the opposite direction, with Australians flagged less often than the control, and no uncertainty has been computed for either. No claim about t may be made until speaker clustered intervals and a correction for testing many consonants at once exist.

the_two_references_do_not_create_the_sam.consequence_for_the_sceptical_family: The largest differentials anywhere in the sensitivity family are on the affricate under the British reference, in both non American groups. They are not promoted to findings. They were not pre declared, and the affricate is one of the consonants whose opportunity count moves between references, so the comparison that produces them is not like with like. They are published in full so that a later pre declared analysis can test them properly.
the_two_references_do_not_create_the_sam.statement: Swapping the reference variety changes the expected phone sequence, so it also changes which consonants get a scoring opportunity at all. Only 8 of the 25 consonants keep their opportunity count within two percent across the two references. The t target gains about 28 percent under the British reference and the affricates gain about 9 percent, while the rhotic loses. A cross reference comparison for any consonant outside those eight is not comparing like with like, and an apparent effect there may be the changed denominator rather than the speakers. This was not known when version 1.1.0 was written, and it withdraws the support for one sentence in it, that the t gap nearly disappears under the repaired reference.

d̪.evidence: The aligner transcribes the, that and this with d̪ at 0.99 probability, and the model uses ð for exactly those words. Mapping on symbol shape rather than function mis-expected the most frequent consonant context in English, which is why d was flagged in roughly half of about 1,300 opportunities.

ɫ.evidence: The frozen model emits ɫ zero times across 25 clips while emitting l 28 times. The token exists in the vocabulary and the model never uses it for English, so expecting it guaranteed a flag: 100.0 percent of ɫ opportunities were flagged in all three speaker groups.

ɫ̩.evidence: Follows the ɫ correction, since it resolved to the same unusable token.

1.1.0.prompted_by: the version 1.0.0 probe run, whose report is retained at .research_data/speech_sound_patterns/variety-probe/report-mapping-v1.0.0.json, SHA256 392c610d4cc1c87bda283e0cf4696afe5a614b95c48c5a4417a3525cbfa445c5

c.evidence: Flagged in 419 of 419 American reference opportunities and 336 of 336 British reference opportunities, at an identical 100.0 percent in the American control and in both comparison groups. The aligner writes the palatal stop for the velar stop before a front vowel. This is the dark l situation exactly: the token is in the model vocabulary and the model never uses it for English.

cʰ.evidence: Follows the c correction. Aspiration is predictable in a stressed onset and was already treated that way for the plain velar stop.

cʷ.evidence: Previously resolved to c, which is itself unusable, so the labialisation entry inherited the defect rather than fixing it.

ç.evidence: Flagged in 611 of 612 American reference opportunities, 99.8 percent, and 398 of 398 under the British reference. The palatal fricative is h before a front vowel, as in him and adhere. The checkpoint 22E8 secondary analysis excluded the other four palatals and missed this one.

ɟ.evidence: Flagged in 308 of 308 American reference opportunities and 155 of 155 British reference opportunities, at 100.0 percent in every speaker group. The voiced counterpart of the c correction.

ɟʷ.evidence: Previously resolved to ɟ, which is itself unusable, so the labialisation entry inherited the defect.

ɲ.evidence: Flagged in 756 of 760 American reference opportunities, 99.5 percent, and at 100.0 percent in the Australian group. The palatal nasal is the alveolar nasal before a front vowel.

ʎ.evidence: Flagged in 857 of 857 American reference opportunities and 747 of 747 British reference opportunities, at 100.0 percent in every group. The palatal lateral is l before a front vowel.

1.2.0.note: These five phone families and the glottal stop together supplied 38.9 percent of every flag the version 1.1.0 probe produced. Because they hit every speaker group at the same rate, they did not fake an accent difference directly. They inflated the baseline and, through differences in how often each group's prompts contained them, distorted the per consonant comparison that the checkpoint reported as its headline finding. The normalisation table in speech_sound_patterns/prompt_pack.py had already recorded the correct target for all five, with a written reason each, one checkpoint later. It was never applied back to the probe.
1.2.0.prompted_by: the 2026-08-22 direction change audit, which re-derived every published probe figure from the retained per clip evidence and found that most flags came from phones the model never produces for English. The superseded report is retained at .research_data/speech_sound_patterns/variety-probe/report-mapping-v1.1.0.json, SHA256 8156ce119af6b879b37f70b30a132fffab130e3e93638c2d41fa32043b856ee8

aggregation_change.what_changed: The per consonant analysis now computes a rate per speaker and then averages, matching the group level analysis. Version 1.1.0 pooled every token in the group and applied no speaker clustering at all.

consonant_inclusion.a_consequence_worth_stating_plainly: The excluded flap is the phone that carries American t flapping, which is a genuine and well documented variety difference. This design cannot test it, because the prompts did not supply enough chances in enough speakers. That is a limit of this probe rather than evidence about flapping, and it belongs in the report beside rhoticity as a second thing this method cannot see.
consonant_inclusion.rule: A consonant enters a per consonant family only if, in each of the two groups being contrasted, it has at least 100 scoring opportunities and at least 50 speakers with at least one opportunity.

detectable_effect.standing_limit: The Australian eligible pool is 674 speakers and the probe already samples about 45 percent of it, so this is not fixable by collecting more Australian speakers.
detectable_effect.what_this_means: The smallest true difference this design would detect four times in five. A differential smaller than this is not evidence of no difference; it is a look too small to tell.

family_A_primary_per_consonant.content: the australian minus american differential, per consonant, under the american reference, at threshold minus one
family_A_primary_per_consonant.why_this_is_the_family_that_matters: This is the exact comparison in which t was selected as the largest per consonant differential. The multiplicity risk was created by choosing one consonant out of the set after seeing all of them, so the set is the family that must control it.
family_A_primary_per_consonant.why_threshold_minus_one: The parent report already designates threshold minus one as the per consonant reporting threshold, in the field per_consonant_rates_at_threshold_minus_one. It is inherited, not chosen now.

family_B_secondary_per_consonant.content: the british minus american differential, per consonant, under the american reference, at threshold minus one
family_B_secondary_per_consonant.why_separate_from_family_A: It is a distinct pre declared contrast with its own directional prediction in the parent contract, and it is the informative middle case rather than the target of the probe. Correcting it inside family A would let the two contrasts borrow evidence from each other.

content: australian minus american under the american reference
british minus american under the american reference
american control change under the repair
family_G_pre_registered_group_level.why_a_separate_family_from_the_consonant: These hypotheses were pre registered before the run. The per consonant analysis was not, and its headline consonant was chosen after seeing which one was largest. Pooling a pre registered test with an exploratory selection would penalise the pre registered one for the other's freedom, and would let the exploratory one hide inside it.
family_G_pre_registered_group_level.why_these_five: They are exactly the two directional predictions the parent contract declared before any speaker was scored: that both non American groups are flagged more under the American reference, and that under the British reference both non American groups fall while the American control stays roughly in place.

family_S_sceptical_sensitivity.content: every per consonant differential in the full grid: included consonants times two contrasts times two references times five thresholds
family_S_sceptical_sensitivity.status: reported, never used to promote a finding that failed family A
family_S_sceptical_sensitivity.why_it_is_reported_regardless_of_outcome: A reader who rejects the argument that thresholds and references are sensitivity dimensions should not have to take this contract's word for it. The harshest defensible family is computed and published whatever it shows, so that declaring the primary family cannot be mistaken for choosing the lenient answer.

not_family_members.the_british_reference_condition: The paired second condition of a single design, not a second hunt. Its job is to show whether a differential shrinks when the reference variety is repaired.
not_family_members.the_five_thresholds: A sensitivity analysis of one hypothesis at nested cutoffs on the same evidence, reported as a curve. They are not five independent chances to find an effect, and no consonant was chosen by looking across them.
not_family_members.the_honest_caveat: Both exclusions are judgements. They are declared here so that a reader can disagree with them, and the sensitivity family below reports what a reader who does disagree would see.

family_definitions.rule: Every family below is fixed by this contract. A p value may not be moved between families, and no family may be split or merged after an outcome is seen.

method.between_group_test: speaker label permutation, conditioned on which speakers had an opportunity
method.interval: speaker clustered bias corrected and accelerated bootstrap, percentile interval reported beside it
method.pairing: one resample serves every reference, threshold and consonant
method.re_inference: none. Stored per target scores only.
method.stratification: within source, at the observed 300 speakers per source
method.within_group_test: paired sign flip permutation across the two references

reference_opportunity_parity.rule: A consonant is treated as comparable across references only when neither group's opportunity count moves by more than two percent. Above that the denominator itself changed and a cross reference difference cannot be attributed to the speakers.

training_lineage_declaration.how_it_would_actually_be_resolved: A second phone recognition model with no Common Voice lineage, rescoring the same 2,400 clips, so the differential can be compared across two models that do not share the evaluation data. That is a fresh inference pass and a new model manifest, so it is recorded as a deferred item rather than performed inside R2.
training_lineage_declaration.the_declaration_in_one_line: Direction unknown, plausibly favours the control group, and the observed result runs against it. The null result is therefore conservative rather than suspect.
training_lineage_declaration.the_overlap: The scoring model facebook/wav2vec2-lv-60-espeak-cv-ft is fine tuned on Common Voice, and this probe evaluates entirely on Common Voice release 26 speakers. speech_sound_patterns/engineering-plan.md disqualifies Wav2Vec2 CommonPhone from counting toward a selection gate for precisely this reason, and the rule was never applied to the probe's own scoring model.
training_lineage_declaration.what_actually_protects_the_finding: The direction. At threshold minus one under the American reference the American control is flagged more often than the Australian group, 0.0863 against 0.0823, which is the opposite of what lineage bias predicts. If the bias is present it works against the observed result rather than producing it.
training_lineage_declaration.what_this_does_not_license: It does not make the evidence independent, it does not let this probe count toward any selection gate, and it does not transfer to a future result that runs the other way. A differential in the direction lineage bias predicts would be uninterpretable under this same reasoning.
training_lineage_declaration.why_the_same_model_scoring_all_groups_do: It does not. Common Voice English is heavily skewed toward American and British contributors, so a model fine tuned on it has plausibly been exposed to far more of the control group's speech than of the Australian group's. That would fit the control better and flag it less, which is a group dependent effect and not a uniform one. Any claim that the overlap cancels because one model scored everybody is wrong and is not made here.

what_this_cannot_establish: That the system correctly detects a genuine Australian mispronunciation. There is still no expert produced Australian phone truth, at any licence and at any price.
Any accuracy, sensitivity or specificity figure, because there is still no truth to measure against.
That a differential surviving correction is a real property of Australian English rather than of these prompts, this corpus, this model or this GOP formulation.
That an interval excluding zero means an effect worth acting on. Nothing here selects, gates or releases anything.

That the system correctly detects a genuine Australian mispronunciation. No Australian expert phone labels exist in this project or, so far as the 2026-07-28 search could establish, in any commercially usable form anywhere.
Any accuracy, sensitivity or specificity figure, because there is no truth to measure against.
That any candidate system, threshold or reference is fit for selection or release.
